response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **terminal-prefix candidate-softmax training** for the supplied BERT4Rec. This is a testable proposal; no validation improvement has been measured.

**Insights.** From the starting point: (1) terminal prefixes match appended-mask inference and emphasize recent context; (2) title-confusable negatives could distinguish specific matches from broad similarity, but may be valid alternatives; (3) preserving ordinary Cloze examples retains supervision across histories. From related work: (1) BERT4Rec already uses final-item masking, so novelty lies in the experimental recipe; (2) gSASRec motivates testing loss calibration, although its evidence concerns another backbone; (3) sampled-softmax research warns that nonuniform sampling requires careful probability treatment. These suggest three directions: inference alignment, competitive ranking, and temporal relevance.

**Framework.** Organize methods by the component they change:

| Component | Foundation | Proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Training context | BERT4Rec Cloze/final masking | Mix Cloze and truncated terminal prefixes |
| Ranking objective | gSASRec; sampled-softmax analysis | Uniform multi-negative candidate softmax |
| Attention | MEANTIME; TiSASRec | Learned relative-position/time biases |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are O/F/U/M/D: originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

- **Terminal-prefix candidate softmax: 4/8/8/8/3.** O: useful combination; established components. F: reusable recipe; gains may saturate. U: emphasizes recent direct connections and discrimination among plausible alternatives; cannot establish ownership or compatibility. M: targets weak competitive separation; training margins may not predict HR@10. D: local sampler/loss changes; requires careful masking.
- **Temporal attention biases: 5/7/7/5/6.** O: adapts known temporal mechanisms; limited conceptual novelty. F: potentially transferable; sparse timestamps limit learning. U: distinguishes recent from stale evidence; gaps do not prove fulfilled needs. M: conditions representations on time; diagnostics do not establish a temporal defect. D: manageable attention changes; predictor and timestamp plumbing expand scope.
- **Moderate title-negative sampling: 4/6/7/7/5.** O: practical semantic adaptation; familiar mining strategy. F: targets confusable items; false negatives constrain scale. U: challenges broad similarity; titles cannot verify compatibility. M: strengthens difficult comparisons; noisy negatives can degrade learning. D: reproducible token retrieval is feasible; filtering needs care.

**Selected algorithm.** Retain one BERT4Rec per category. Mix ordinary Cloze supervision with training-only prefixes whose terminal target is replaced by MASK and whose later interactions are removed. Optimize candidate softmax against multiple uniform negatives.

This explicitly targets two observed user failures: older isolated interests competing with recent repeated behavior, and broadly plausible items outranking direct matches. It targets Electronics’ weakest sampled separation (6.62% negative-beats-positive rate), without treating that statistic as validation HR@10. Ownership and exact compatibility remain unobserved.

Keep seeds, splits, routing, 200-epoch ceiling and 200 batches/epoch fixed. Compare against the corrected baseline using pinned macro validation HR@10; retain unchanged diagnostic definitions and predictor architecture consistency.

idea.description: Train each category’s single BERT4Rec with a mixture of ordinary masked-item reconstruction and terminal-prefix candidate-softmax examples. Use uniform multiple negatives initially, avoiding semantic mining until the training-objective hypothesis has been evaluated.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies excessive reliance on broad similarity and insufficient priority for recent repeated behavior. Terminal prefixes train the precise next-choice context, while multiple competing candidates give the model an opportunity to learn finer discrimination. Electronics has the weakest measured sampled separation, but these training diagnostics neither establish the cause nor predict host HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Apply this change inside the supplied corrected baseline rather than replacing its data pipeline or backbone. Suggested initial settings are 50% terminal-prefix examples, 50% ordinary Cloze examples, 64 uniform negatives per supervised target, and temperature 1.0. These are proposed settings, not measured optima. Sample terminal targets only from training interactions, with at least one preceding interaction. Remove the suffix and replace the target with the reserved MASK; never supply its identity as input. Exclude the target and known training positives from negative sampling; if no eligible negatives exist, skip that supervised position. Treat the objective as candidate classification, without claiming an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimate. Preserve baseline optimizer and architecture to isolate the training change. Read the final nonpadding position using explicit indices, never nonpadding_count-1 on left padding. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200 and 200 batches per epoch. Retain all four category routes, exactly one trained checkpoint per category, and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnostic batches must continue to expose valid masked-position targets with the original definitions. Inference must append MASK after the retained history and load the same architecture through the predictor writer. No architecture modification is required for this proposal. Select by the host’s pinned macro validation HR@10; do not consult test labels or other trials.
idea.pseudocode:
Configuration proposal: terminal_probability=0.5; negatives_per_target=64.
For each category, initialize one corrected baseline BERT4Rec with seed 42.
For each permitted training batch:
    For each sampled training history:
        With probability terminal_probability:
            Choose a training target index t >= 1 using the baseline seeded RNG.
            sequence = left_pad((history[:t] + [MASK])[-max_length:])
            positive = history[t] at the terminal MASK position only.
        Otherwise:
            sequence, positive = baseline family-specific Cloze masking(history).
        Sample uniform eligible negatives for every supervised MASK position.
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    For each supervised position:
        candidates = [positive] + sampled_negatives
        logits = model.predict_score(position_features, candidates)
        position_loss = cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0)
    loss = mean(position_loss)
    Perform one baseline optimizer update.
Use the existing validation/checkpoint protocol without checkpoint averaging.
Save one checkpoint per category and emit its matching appended-MASK predictor.

originality.positive: Combines inference-aligned contexts and competitive ranking into a small, controlled BERT4Rec experiment.
originality.negative: Final-item masking and sampled candidate objectives are established techniques; novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: Provides a simple foundation for subsequent temporal or semantic ablations if validation supports the hypothesis.
future_potential.negative: It cannot recover unobserved ownership, compatibility requirements or current intent, and benefits may saturate.

code_difficulty.positive: Primarily changes supervised-example construction and loss computation while preserving architecture and inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful handling of terminal truncation, left padding, valid negatives and diagnostic compatibility.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses final-item masking to better align training with next-item inference.
limitations: Already establishes final-item masking, limiting novelty of the proposed context mixture.
Does not establish the best masking mixture or candidate objective for this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Examines overconfidence and optimization problems associated with negative-sampled BCE.
limitations: Its backbone-specific findings motivate a BERT4Rec loss experiment but do not establish that candidate softmax will improve this task.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis for recommendation
contributions: Analyzes sampling bias and differences between always-included positives and sampled negatives.
limitations: Does not make a small uniform candidate objective equivalent to full-catalog cross-entropy.
Does not establish the optimal negative count for the supplied datasets.

related_work.title: MEANTIME
contributions: Provides a precedent for multiple temporal embeddings and differentiated attention within one jointly trained model.
limitations: Temporal modeling requires a consistent unknown-time convention for the inference mask.
Observed time gaps do not establish ownership, fulfillment or current demand.
